# litellm_fallback (Resource)

The `litellm_fallback` resource allows you to configure model fallback configurations separately from the general router configuration. This provides a cleaner and safer way to manage fallbacks for individual models.

## Prerequisites

- Database storage must be enabled: Set `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True` in your environment
- Models must exist in the router before configuring fallbacks

## Example Usage

### General Fallback

```terraform
resource "litellm_fallback" "general" {
  model           = "gpt-3.5-turbo"
  fallback_models = ["gpt-4", "claude-3-haiku"]
  fallback_type   = "general"
}
```

### Context Window Fallback

```terraform
resource "litellm_fallback" "context_window" {
  model           = "gpt-3.5-turbo"
  fallback_models = ["gpt-4-32k", "claude-3-opus"]
  fallback_type   = "context_window"
}
```

### Content Policy Fallback

```terraform
resource "litellm_fallback" "content_policy" {
  model           = "gpt-4"
  fallback_models = ["claude-3-haiku"]
  fallback_type   = "content_policy"
}
```

### Multiple Fallback Configurations

```terraform
# General fallback for GPT-4o
resource "litellm_fallback" "gpt4o_fallback" {
  model           = "gpt-4o"
  fallback_models = ["gpt-4o-azure", "gpt-4-turbo", "claude-3-sonnet"]
  fallback_type   = "general"
}

# Context window fallback for GPT-4o
resource "litellm_fallback" "gpt4o_context_fallback" {
  model           = "gpt-4o"
  fallback_models = ["claude-3-sonnet", "claude-3-opus"]
  fallback_type   = "context_window"
}

# Embedding model fallback
resource "litellm_fallback" "embedding_fallback" {
  model           = "text-embedding-ada-002"
  fallback_models = ["text-embedding-ada-002-azure", "text-embedding-3-small"]
  fallback_type   = "general"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `model` (String) The primary model name to configure fallbacks for.
- `fallback_models` (List of String) List of fallback model names in priority order.

### Optional

- `fallback_type` (String) Type of fallback. Options: `general` (default), `context_window`, `content_policy`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the fallback configuration (combination of model and fallback_type).

## Fallback Types

### general

Standard fallbacks for any error. This is the most common type of fallback and is triggered when a model is unavailable, rate-limited, or returns an error.

### context_window

Specifically triggered when a context window exceeded error occurs. Use this when the input is too long for the primary model and you want to fallback to a model with a larger context window.

### content_policy

Specifically triggered when content policy violations occur. Use this when the primary model rejects content due to safety filters and you want to fallback to a model with different content policies.

## Import

Fallback configurations can be imported using the model name and fallback type, separated by a colon:

```shell
# Import general fallback for gpt-3.5-turbo
terraform import litellm_fallback.example gpt-3.5-turbo:general

# Import context_window fallback for gpt-3.5-turbo
terraform import litellm_fallback.example gpt-3.5-turbo:context_window

# Import content_policy fallback for gpt-4
terraform import litellm_fallback.example gpt-4:content_policy
```

## Notes

- Each model can have multiple fallback configurations (one per fallback_type)
- Fallbacks are attempted in the order specified in `fallback_models`
- The maximum number of fallbacks attempted is controlled by the router's `max_fallbacks` setting
- Changes take effect immediately and are persisted to the database
- The LiteLLM API validates that both the primary model and fallback models exist in the router
